subs.label: Movements & Schools
subs.axis: Axis: by named movement or school, in rough order of emergence; Slow Cinema, a transnational style, last.

leaves.label: German Expressionism
leaves.defn: A film of the Weimar Expressionist movement: painted, distorted décor, chiaroscuro and stylised acting expressing inner states (The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari, Nosferatu, Metropolis). Later Expressionist-influenced genre films go to their genre (A4 Horror).
leaves.see: A1-2 French Impressionist Cinema; A4 Horror

leaves.label: French Impressionist Cinema
leaves.defn: A film of the 1919–1929 French avant-garde narrative school (Gance, Epstein, Dulac) using rhythmic montage and subjective optical effects to render feeling (J'accuse!, Napoleon, The Fall of the House of Usher).
leaves.see: A1-1 German Expressionism; A21-15 Avant-Garde Short

leaves.label: Soviet Montage
leaves.defn: A Soviet silent film built on montage theory, meaning made by the collision of shots (Battleship Potemkin, Strike, Earth). Vertov's documentary Man with a Movie Camera sits in A19-3.
leaves.see: A19-3 City Symphony

leaves.label: Poetic Realism
leaves.defn: A 1930s French film of fatalistic working-class romance in studio-built, mist-laden settings (Port of Shadows, L'Atalante, Daybreak).
leaves.see: A1-5 Italian Neorealism; A2 Crime

leaves.label: Italian Neorealism
leaves.defn: A postwar Italian film shot on location with non-professional actors about poverty and reconstruction (Bicycle Thieves, Rome, Open City, Umberto D.).
leaves.see: A1-6 Parallel Cinema; A16 Drama

leaves.label: Parallel Cinema
leaves.defn: An Indian art-cinema film of the realist, non-commercial alternative to the mainstream, from Ray and Ghatak onward (Pather Panchali, Charulata, The Cloud-Capped Star). Popular Hindi cinema goes to A18.
leaves.see: A1-5 Italian Neorealism; A18 Popular Cinema Modes

leaves.label: Polish Film School
leaves.defn: A Polish film of 1955–1961 reckoning with war and resistance (Ashes and Diamonds, Kanal, A Generation).
leaves.see: A1-25 Cinema of Moral Anxiety; A9 War Film

leaves.label: French New Wave
leaves.defn: A film by the late-1950s/1960s Cahiers-generation directors breaking classical continuity: location shooting, jump cuts, cinephile reference (The 400 Blows, Breathless, Jules and Jim). The Resnais–Marker–Varda wing with literary modernist leanings goes to A1-9.
leaves.see: A1-9 Left Bank; A1-31 Cinéma du look
leaves.axis: by phase of the movement: forerunners and first features, high period, late and politicised films

leaves.label: Left Bank
leaves.defn: A film of the Rive Gauche group (Resnais, Marker, Varda, Duras) joining literary modernism to fractured memory and time (Hiroshima Mon Amour, Last Year at Marienbad, Muriel).
leaves.see: A1-8 French New Wave; A19-4 Essay Film

leaves.label: British New Wave
leaves.defn: A British film of c.1959–1970 adapting kitchen-sink realism to working-class lives in the industrial North (Saturday Night and Sunday Morning, A Taste of Honey, Kes).
leaves.see: A16 Drama

leaves.label: Japanese New Wave
leaves.defn: A Japanese film of the 1960s–70s nūberu bāgu breaking with studio humanism through sex, politics and formal rupture (Death by Hanging, Woman in the Dunes, The Insect Woman).
leaves.see: A1-8 French New Wave; A20 Experimental & Avant-Garde

leaves.label: Czechoslovak New Wave
leaves.defn: A Czechoslovak film of 1963–1970 using absurdist humour, surreal fantasy or non-professional realism against official culture (Daisies, Closely Watched Trains, The Firemen's Ball).
leaves.see: A1-13 Yugoslav Black Wave

leaves.label: Yugoslav Black Wave
leaves.defn: A Yugoslav film of the 1960s–early 1970s whose dark, sexually frank critique of socialist society drew censure (WR: Mysteries of the Organism, I Even Met Happy Gypsies, Early Works).
leaves.see: A1-12 Czechoslovak New Wave

leaves.label: Portuguese New Cinema
leaves.defn: A film of the 1960s Novo Cinema in Portugal, modernist breaks with the Estado Novo studio tradition (The Green Years, Change of Life).
leaves.see: A1-8 French New Wave

leaves.label: New German Cinema
leaves.defn: A West German film of the 1960s–early 1980s auteur renewal after the Oberhausen Manifesto (Aguirre, the Wrath of God, Fear Eats the Soul, Kings of the Road).
leaves.see: A1-36 Berlin School

leaves.label: Cinema Novo
leaves.defn: A Brazilian film of the 1960s movement of "an idea in the head and a camera in the hand", poverty, violence and myth in the sertão (Black God, White Devil, Barren Lives, Entranced Earth).
leaves.see: A1-17 Cinema Marginal; A1-18 Third Cinema

leaves.label: Cinema Marginal
leaves.defn: A Brazilian underground film of the late 1960s, a trash-aesthetic, anarchic reply to Cinema Novo (The Red Light Bandit).
leaves.aliases: Cinema de Boca do Lixo, udigrudi
leaves.see: A1-16 Cinema Novo; A20-2 Underground Film

leaves.label: Third Cinema
leaves.defn: A militant anti-colonial film of the Latin American, African and Arab "third cinema" manifesto against Hollywood and auteur cinema (The Battle of Algiers, Memories of Underdevelopment, Blood of the Condor). Its militant documentaries sit in A19.
leaves.see: A1-16 Cinema Novo; A19-4 Essay Film

leaves.label: New American Cinema
leaves.defn: A New York independent film of the late-1950s/1960s New American Cinema Group, improvised and anti-Hollywood (Shadows, The Cool World). Its underground and diary films sit in A20-2 and A19-5.
leaves.see: A20-2 Underground Film; A1-20 New Hollywood

leaves.label: New Hollywood
leaves.defn: An American studio-era film of 1967–1980 made by the auteur generation that took over Hollywood, with downbeat endings, sex, violence and European influence (Bonnie and Clyde, Taxi Driver, Nashville, Jaws).
leaves.see: A2 Crime; A1-19 New American Cinema
leaves.axis: by the strand of the movement: counterculture, crime revision, paranoia and horror, character studies, Vietnam and late epics; the blockbuster turn last

leaves.label: L.A. Rebellion
leaves.defn: A film by the Black filmmakers of UCLA's 1967–1990s L.A. School, neorealist and Third Cinema-informed (Killer of Sheep, Daughters of the Dust, Bush Mama).
leaves.see: A1-18 Third Cinema

leaves.label: No Wave Cinema
leaves.defn: A late-1970s/1980s Lower East Side underground film, punk, Super 8 or 16mm, deadpan (Stranger Than Paradise, Permanent Vacation, Born in Flames).
leaves.see: A20-2 Underground Film

leaves.label: Australian New Wave
leaves.defn: An Australian film of the 1970s–early 1980s revival, landscape-haunted and period-set (Picnic at Hanging Rock, Wake in Fright, Breaker Morant).
leaves.see: A8 Historical & Period Film

leaves.label: Second Golden Age of Philippine Cinema
leaves.defn: A Filipino film of the 1970s–early 1980s auteur renaissance under martial law (Manila in the Claws of Light, Insiang, Oro, Plata, Mata).
leaves.see: A1-39 Slow Cinema

leaves.label: Cinema of Moral Anxiety
leaves.defn: A Polish film of 1976–1981 probing compromise and corruption in socialist life (Camera Buff, Man of Iron, Blind Chance).
leaves.see: A1-7 Polish Film School

leaves.label: Iranian New Wave
leaves.defn: An Iranian art film from the late 1960s onward, often child-centred, reflexive and near-documentary (Close-Up, Taste of Cherry, The White Balloon, A Separation).
leaves.see: A1-39 Slow Cinema; A19-7 Docufiction

leaves.label: Taiwan New Cinema
leaves.defn: A Taiwanese film of the 1980s–90s movement of long takes and historical memory (A City of Sadness, Yi Yi, A Brighter Summer Day).
leaves.see: A1-39 Slow Cinema; A1-28 Hong Kong New Wave

leaves.label: Hong Kong New Wave
leaves.defn: A Hong Kong film of the late-1970s/1980s new wave and its second wave (Boat People, Rouge, Chungking Express).
leaves.see: A1-27 Taiwan New Cinema

leaves.label: Fifth Generation
leaves.defn: A mainland Chinese film by the 1982 Beijing Film Academy graduates, allegorical and visually lavish (Yellow Earth, Red Sorghum, Farewell My Concubine).
leaves.see: A1-30 Sixth Generation

leaves.label: Sixth Generation
leaves.defn: A mainland Chinese film of the 1990s–2000s urban, semi-underground generation (Platform, Suzhou River, Still Life).
leaves.see: A1-29 Fifth Generation; A1-39 Slow Cinema

leaves.label: Cinéma du look
leaves.defn: A 1980s French film of glossy, youth-oriented, music-video visual style (Diva, Subway, Betty Blue).
leaves.see: A1-8 French New Wave

leaves.label: New Queer Cinema
leaves.defn: An early-1990s independent queer film, defiant and formally transgressive in the AIDS era (Poison, My Own Private Idaho, The Living End).
leaves.see: A19-4 Essay Film; A13 Romance

leaves.label: New Argentine Cinema
leaves.defn: An Argentine film of the 1990s–2000s renewal, minimalist and observational (The Swamp, Pizza, Beer, and Cigarettes, Los Muertos).
leaves.see: A1-39 Slow Cinema

leaves.label: Dogme 95
leaves.defn: A film certified under the Dogme 95 "vow of chastity": handheld, location sound, no added lighting or score (The Celebration, The Idiots, Julien Donkey-Boy).
leaves.see: A1-35 Mumblecore

leaves.label: Mumblecore
leaves.defn: A 2000s–2010s American micro-budget film of improvised talk among twenty-somethings (Funny Ha Ha, Drinking Buddies, Tiny Furniture).
leaves.see: A1-34 Dogme 95; A12 Comedy

leaves.label: Berlin School
leaves.defn: A German art film of the 1990s–2010s Berliner Schule, restrained and observational (Yella, Everyone Else, Toni Erdmann).
leaves.see: A1-15 New German Cinema

leaves.label: Romanian New Wave
leaves.defn: A Romanian film of the 2000s onward, long-take realist dramas of post-communist bureaucracy and morality (The Death of Mr. Lazarescu, 4 Months, 3 Weeks and 2 Days, Police, Adjective).
leaves.see: A1-39 Slow Cinema

leaves.label: Greek Weird Wave
leaves.defn: A Greek film of the 2009–2010s crisis-era wave of deadpan, absurdist family and social allegory (Dogtooth, Attenberg, Alps).
leaves.see: A1-37 Romanian New Wave

leaves.label: Slow Cinema
leaves.defn: A narrative art film whose defining device is duration: very long takes, minimal action, contemplative observation (Jeanne Dielman, Sátántangó, Stalker, Uncle Boonmee). National movements with a slow strand (Taiwan New Cinema, Romanian New Wave) keep their own leaf.
leaves.see: A1-27 Taiwan New Cinema; A20-3 Structural Film
leaves.axis: by lineage and region: European modernist precursors first, then later European, Asian, Turkish and Ibero-American practitioners

subs.label: Documentary
subs.axis: Axis: by documentary mode first (observational, ethnographic, poetic, essay, personal, archival, hybrid, propaganda), then by subject (politics, investigation, crime, war, history, people, art, cinema, music, sport, travel, nature); mondo last.

leaves.label: Direct Cinema & Cinéma Vérité
leaves.defn: A documentary made by observing events as they happen, with lightweight sync-sound cameras, no narration and minimal intervention (Primary, Titicut Follies, Salesman, Grey Gardens). A first-person or reflexive film goes to A19-5; a film staging or re-enacting goes to A19-7.
leaves.see: A19-2 Ethnographic Film; A19-7 Docufiction
leaves.axis: by what the camera watches: institutions, campaigns and public life, families and private lives, work, then communities and places

leaves.label: Ethnographic Film
leaves.defn: A documentary that records and interprets a culture or way of life, from Flaherty to sensory ethnography (Nanook of the North, Dead Birds, Leviathan, Manakamana).
leaves.see: A19-1 Direct Cinema & Cinéma Vérité; A19-7 Docufiction

leaves.label: City Symphony
leaves.defn: A feature-length silent-era documentary portraying a city's day as a rhythmic montage (Berlin: Symphony of a Metropolis, Man with a Movie Camera). City-symphony shorts sit in A21-12.
leaves.see: A21-12 Documentary Short; A20-5 Non-Narrative Film

leaves.label: Essay Film
leaves.defn: A documentary that argues or meditates in a personal voice, usually through first-person narration over assembled images (Sans Soleil, F for Fake, The Gleaners & I, I Am Not Your Negro). When the subject is the filmmaker's own life the film goes to A19-5.
leaves.see: A19-5 Diary Film; A19-6 Compilation Film
leaves.axis: by the essay's object: images and cinema, history and politics, place, then identity and the body

leaves.label: Diary Film
leaves.defn: A first-person documentary whose subject is the filmmaker's own life and family, often diaristic or home-movie based (Reminiscences of a Journey to Lithuania, Sherman's March, Tarnation, Stories We Tell).
leaves.aliases: personal documentary, autobiographical documentary, first-person documentary
leaves.see: A19-4 Essay Film

leaves.label: Compilation Film
leaves.defn: A documentary built mainly from pre-existing archival footage, edited without new interviews (The Atomic Cafe, Apollo 11, They Shall Not Grow Old, State Funeral). Artist appropriation of footage goes to A20-4.
leaves.see: A20-4 Found-Footage Film; A19-13 Historical Documentary

leaves.label: Docufiction
leaves.defn: A film that blends documentary and fiction: staged or re-enacted scenes with real people, or fiction shot as documentary (Louisiana Story, Caesar Must Die, Four Daughters, The Arbor). Includes mockumentary features.
leaves.see: A19-1 Direct Cinema & Cinéma Vérité; A19-2 Ethnographic Film

leaves.label: Propaganda Film
leaves.defn: A documentary made by or for a state or cause to persuade a mass audience (Triumph of the Will, Why We Fight, The Negro Soldier). Wartime sponsored shorts go to A21-14.
leaves.see: A21-14 Sponsored Film; A19-12 War Documentary

leaves.label: Political Documentary
leaves.defn: A documentary that takes a side on a public issue or follows a political movement, campaign or politician (Roger & Me, Harlan County U.S.A., An Inconvenient Truth, 13th). Exposés of hidden wrongdoing go to A19-10.
leaves.aliases: advocacy documentary, activist documentary, social-issue documentary
leaves.see: A19-10 Investigative Documentary; A19-8 Propaganda Film
leaves.axis: by the cause: first-person polemic, environment and food, labour, civil rights, gender and LGBTQ movements, then elections, politicians and protest

leaves.label: Investigative Documentary
leaves.defn: A documentary that uncovers concealed wrongdoing through journalistic investigation (Inside Job, Citizenfour, Going Clear, Collective). A criminal case goes to A19-11.
leaves.see: A19-11 True Crime Documentary; A19-9 Political Documentary
leaves.axis: by the target of the investigation: corporations, the state, cults and belief, disasters, then media and technology

leaves.label: True Crime Documentary
leaves.defn: A documentary reconstructing a specific crime, its investigation or trial (The Thin Blue Line, Paradise Lost, Capturing the Friedmans, The Tinder Swindler).
leaves.see: A19-10 Investigative Documentary; A2 Crime
leaves.axis: by the kind of case: murder and violent crime, trials and wrongful convictions, fraud and hoaxes, then abuse and exploitation

leaves.label: War Documentary
leaves.defn: A documentary filmed in or about a war or armed conflict, often from the front line (Restrepo, For Sama, 20 Days in Mariupol, Hearts and Minds). Archival war compilations go to A19-6; wartime state films to A19-8.
leaves.see: A19-8 Propaganda Film; A9 War Film

leaves.label: Historical Documentary
leaves.defn: A documentary reconstructing a past event or period through testimony and research (Shoah, The Act of Killing, Freedom Riders, The Fog of War).
leaves.see: A19-6 Compilation Film; A19-12 War Documentary

leaves.label: Biographical Documentary
leaves.defn: A documentary portrait of one person, or of a small group or subculture, other than a musician, artist, filmmaker or athlete (Won't You Be My Neighbor?, RBG, Gates of Heaven, Paris Is Burning).
leaves.see: A19-15 Art Documentary; A19-17 Rockumentary; A11 Biographical Film
leaves.axis: by the subject: entertainers, public figures and thinkers, ordinary lives and eccentrics, then subcultures

leaves.label: Art Documentary
leaves.defn: A documentary about a visual artist, designer, architect, dancer or fashion house and their work (Crumb, Pina, Finding Vivian Maier, Exit Through the Gift Shop).
leaves.see: A19-14 Biographical Documentary; A19-16 Making-of & Film History Documentary

leaves.label: Making-of & Film History Documentary
leaves.defn: A documentary about cinema or television itself: the making of a production, a filmmaker or actor portrait, or a history of films (Hearts of Darkness, Burden of Dreams, Jodorowsky's Dune, The Celluloid Closet).
leaves.see: A19-4 Essay Film; A19-15 Art Documentary
leaves.axis: by focus: one production, one filmmaker or actor, then film history and criticism

leaves.label: Rockumentary
leaves.defn: A documentary about musicians or music, built on interviews, archive and backstage footage rather than a complete performance (Dont Look Back, Amy, Searching for Sugar Man, Buena Vista Social Club). A film of a performance goes to A19-18.
leaves.see: A19-18 Concert Film; A14 Musical & Dance Film
leaves.axis: by subject: an artist's life, a star's self-portrait or tour, a band or recording, then scenes and roots music

leaves.label: Concert Film
leaves.defn: A film whose substance is a recorded live performance, concert, tour show or festival (Monterey Pop, The Last Waltz, Stop Making Sense, Taylor Swift: The Eras Tour).
leaves.see: A19-17 Rockumentary; B16 Live Event & Sports Television
leaves.axis: by the performance: festivals, rock and soul concerts, pop arena tours, then stage and studio performances

leaves.label: Sports Documentary
leaves.defn: A documentary about an athlete, team, match or competition (When We Were Kings, Senna, Hoop Dreams, The King of Kong). Official Olympic films go to A19-20.
leaves.see: A19-20 Olympic Film; A19-22 Mountaineering Film

leaves.label: Olympic Film
leaves.defn: An official or authorised feature film of an Olympic Games (Olympia, Tokyo Olympiad, Visions of Eight, 16 Days of Glory).
leaves.see: A19-19 Sports Documentary
leaves.axis: by era of the Olympic film: interwar, postwar national and auteur films, then the Greenspan and later era

leaves.label: Travelogue Film
leaves.defn: A documentary organised as a journey through places, recording what the traveller sees (This Is Cinerama, Calcutta, ¡Vivan las antípodas!).
leaves.see: A19-22 Mountaineering Film; A19-4 Essay Film

leaves.label: Mountaineering & Expedition Film
leaves.defn: A documentary of an expedition or feat of endurance in mountains, ice, ocean or wilderness (Kon-Tiki, Touching the Void, Free Solo, The Rescue).
leaves.aliases: mountain film, adventure documentary, expedition film
leaves.see: A19-21 Travelogue Film; A19-19 Sports Documentary

leaves.label: Nature Documentary
leaves.defn: A documentary about animals, plants or the natural world (The Silent World, March of the Penguins, Microcosmos, My Octopus Teacher).
leaves.see: A19-9 Political Documentary; A21-13 Scientific Film

leaves.label: Mondo Film
leaves.defn: A shock documentary of real or staged death, cruelty and taboo customs (Faces of Death, Orozco the Embalmer).
leaves.see: A19-7 Docufiction; A4 Horror

subs.label: Experimental & Avant-Garde
subs.axis: Axis: by avant-garde strategy for feature-length work: dream logic, underground, system, appropriation, tone poem, altered state, then avant-garde narrative.

leaves.label: Surrealist Film
leaves.defn: A film built on Surrealist dream logic, irrational juxtaposition and the disruption of bourgeois order (L'Age d'Or, The Exterminating Angel, The Holy Mountain, Eraserhead). Surrealist shorts sit in A21-15.
leaves.see: A21-15 Avant-Garde Short; A20-6 Psychedelic Film

leaves.label: Underground Film
leaves.defn: A low-budget, self-distributed avant-garde feature made outside the industry, often transgressive or camp (Flaming Creatures, Chelsea Girls, Pink Narcissus, Trash Humpers).
leaves.see: A1-19 New American Cinema; A1-22 No Wave Cinema

leaves.label: Structural Film
leaves.defn: An experimental film whose shape is a predetermined system: fixed camera, duration, repetition or rule (Wavelength, Zorns Lemma, Empire, 13 Lakes).
leaves.see: A1-39 Slow Cinema; A21-15 Avant-Garde Short

leaves.label: Found-Footage Film
leaves.defn: An experimental feature made by re-editing appropriated film material (Decasia, Star Spangled to Death, The Clock). Archival documentary goes to A19-6.
leaves.see: A19-6 Compilation Film

leaves.label: Non-Narrative Film
leaves.defn: A feature without plot or characters, built as an audiovisual tone poem of images and music (Koyaanisqatsi, Baraka, Samsara).
leaves.see: A19-3 City Symphony; A19-23 Nature Documentary

leaves.label: Psychedelic Film
leaves.defn: An experimental feature that simulates altered states through strobing colour, sound and disorientation (Head, Enter the Void, Lux Æterna).
leaves.see: A20-1 Surrealist Film

leaves.label: Art Film
leaves.defn: A narrative feature whose avant-garde form (tableau, recitation, fragmentation, anti-illusion) is its defining element (The Color of Pomegranates, India Song, Russian Ark, Holy Motors). Duration-based art films go to A1-39 Slow Cinema.
leaves.see: A1-39 Slow Cinema; A16 Drama

subs.label: Short Film
subs.axis: Axis: by short-film mode: early cinema forms first, then fiction shorts by genre, then nonfiction shorts by purpose, avant-garde shorts last.

leaves.label: Actuality Film
leaves.defn: A pre-1910 single-shot or few-shot nonfiction film recording a real scene (Workers Leaving the Factory, The Arrival of a Train, Roundhay Garden Scene).
leaves.see: A21-2 Newsreel; A21-3 Trick Film

leaves.label: Newsreel
leaves.defn: A short topical news film for theatrical release (Hindenburg Disaster Newsreel Footage, Tacoma Narrows Bridge Collapse, Faces of November).
leaves.see: A21-1 Actuality Film; A21-12 Documentary Short

leaves.label: Trick Film
leaves.defn: An early short built on camera tricks (stop substitution, multiple exposure) for magical effect (A Trip to the Moon, The India Rubber Head, Dream of a Rarebit Fiend).
leaves.see: A21-1 Actuality Film; A6 Fantasy & Adventure

leaves.label: One-Reeler
leaves.defn: A silent narrative short of one reel or less, the story film of the nickelodeon era (The Great Train Robbery, A Corner in Wheat, The Musketeers of Pig Alley). Silent comedy shorts go to A21-5.
leaves.see: A21-5 Slapstick Short

leaves.label: Slapstick Short
leaves.defn: A silent or early-sound comedy short of physical gags, typically a one- or two-reeler (The Immigrant, One Week, The Music Box).
leaves.see: A21-8 Comedy Short Film; A12 Comedy

leaves.label: Musical Short
leaves.defn: A short whose substance is a song or musical number: early sound musical shorts, soundies and long-form music videos (Black and Tan, Jammin' the Blues, Runaway, Anima).
leaves.see: A19-18 Concert Film; A14 Musical & Dance Film

leaves.label: Drama Short Film
leaves.defn: A live-action fiction short whose engine is drama rather than comedy or genre (The Lunch Date, Wasp, The Present, The Wonderful Story of Henry Sugar).
leaves.see: A21-8 Comedy Short Film; A16 Drama
leaves.axis: by the dramatic engine: social realism, childhood, relationships, art-house and literary, crime, then war

leaves.label: Comedy Short Film
leaves.defn: A sound-era live-action comedy short (Bottle Rocket, Six Shooter, Coffee and Cigarettes, An Irish Goodbye). Silent and early-sound slapstick goes to A21-5.
leaves.see: A21-5 Slapstick Short; A12 Comedy

leaves.label: Horror Short Film
leaves.defn: A live-action horror short (Lights Out, Saw, Tarantella, Frankenweenie).
leaves.see: A4 Horror; A21-10 Science Fiction & Fantasy Short Film

leaves.label: Science Fiction & Fantasy Short Film
leaves.defn: A live-action science-fiction or fantasy short (La Jetée, The Red Balloon, Electronic Labyrinth THX 1138 4EB, Rakka).
leaves.see: A5 Science Fiction; A6 Fantasy & Adventure

leaves.label: Tie-In Short Film
leaves.defn: A short made to extend or promote an existing property or brand: studio one-shots, fan films, fake trailers, commissioned branded shorts (Marvel One-Shot: Agent Carter, Team Thor, Power Rangers, Castello Cavalcanti).
leaves.see: A21-8 Comedy Short Film
leaves.axis: by who made it and why: studio tie-ins, unofficial fan films, then commissioned branded shorts

leaves.label: Documentary Short
leaves.defn: A nonfiction short of the sound era not made as sponsored or scientific film (Night and Fog, Land Without Bread, The House Is Black, Period. End of Sentence.).
leaves.see: A19 Documentary; A21-14 Sponsored Film
leaves.axis: by mode and subject: portraits, political and activist films, city symphonies and poetic shorts, essays and memory, music, then sport

leaves.label: Scientific Film
leaves.defn: A short that films natural or laboratory phenomena for science, often through microcinematography (The Sea Horse, The Vampire, The Love Life of the Octopus).
leaves.see: A19-23 Nature Documentary; A21-14 Sponsored Film

leaves.label: Sponsored Film
leaves.defn: A short commissioned by a government, company or institution to inform, instruct or promote (The Plow That Broke the Plains, Listen to Britain, Duck and Cover, Glass).
leaves.aliases: industrial film, educational film, government film
leaves.see: A19-8 Propaganda Film; A21-12 Documentary Short
leaves.axis: by sponsor: governments and wartime ministries, industry, then educational bodies

leaves.label: Avant-Garde Short
leaves.defn: A short experimental film working with form, perception or the film material rather than story (Meshes of the Afternoon, Ballet Mécanique, Mothlight, Serene Velocity).
leaves.see: A20 Experimental & Avant-Garde
leaves.axis: by avant-garde mode: Dada and cinéma pur, surrealist and trance films, lyrical film, structural film, found footage, then video and expanded work
